scenarios.name: Permanent lunar base
scenarios.objective: Find Earth places where the terrain, materials and thermal behaviour of a lunar south polar base area can be studied, to rehearse site characterization, construction on slopes and mobility around a base.

not_comparable.moon-persistently-lit: no Earth cube at this target's pixel scale (for example 5 m)

similarity.why: buildability and mobility depend on slope first
thermal behaviour of the surface, as a relative quantity

requirements.what: Bearing capacity, boulder density, landing hazards
Which environments the base area spans
requirements.value: lit highlands for the base; persistently lit areas for power; shadowed regions and pits as nearby targets

cannot_assess: Illumination by a Sun grazing the horizon; permanently shadowed cryogenic surfaces.
Regolith mechanics (no layer in the catalogues; E9).
Volatile resources (lunar indicators have no Earth equivalent).
Mass wasting under lunar gravity (only slope is compared).

scenarios.name: Robotic lunar exploration
scenarios.objective: Find Earth terrain whose slope distribution matches a lunar target environment, to test rover mobility, navigation and traverse planning.

similarity.why: the only independent terrain property at 1 km and 40 m (T21)

requirements.what: Slope a crewed lunar rover was designed for
requirements.value: 20 to 23° in favourable conditions, maximum 25° (Apollo LRV)

requirements.what: Slope limit of a polar robotic rover
requirements.value: 15° (VIPER), not stated in the NTRS abstracts read

requirements.what: Share of a window that must be at or below the climbing limit

suitability.why: share of the window at or below 20°

cannot_assess: Obstacles below the DEM pixel (rocks, small craters, the slope under a wheel).
Traction and sinkage in regolith under lunar gravity.
Thermal limits of the lunar night and of shadowed regions.
Communication and navigation conditions (no GNSS on the Moon).
Roughness, until the T41 effective resolution test (context only).
